original.reason: The termwise bound is true, but the AM-GM comparison for n(n-1)...(n-k+1) has the opposite direction: that product is at most its mean to the k-th power. The ensuing conclusion does not follow.

judgment.reason: Its central product lemma is asserted with only a vague reference to a “standard” comparison; no valid derivation is supplied. This is a material missing proof step.
The required consecutive-product inequality is merely labeled classical and attributed vaguely to AM-GM/rearrangement, without proving it. That unsupported lemma is the essential step.
The proof relies entirely on a stated “standard product inequality,” but neither AM-GM nor rearrangement as cited establishes it without further argument. The material gap remains.
The claimed AM-GM/rearrangement comparison for the product of ratios is not demonstrated. Since it is the sole justification of the termwise bound, the proof is incomplete.
